stem: A taxi fare, in dollars, is a linear function of the number of miles driven. A 4-mile ride costs 13.40 dollars, and a 10-mile ride costs 29.00 dollars. What is the greatest whole number of miles a rider can travel if the fare must be no more than 20 dollars?
solution: The cost per mile is \(\frac{29.00 - 13.40}{10 - 4} = \frac{15.60}{6} = 2.60\) dollars.
The fixed part is \(13.40 - 4(2.60) = 3\) dollars, so the fare is \(2.6m + 3\).
\(2.6m + 3 \le 20\) gives \(m \le \frac{17}{2.6} \approx 6.54\), so the greatest whole number of miles is 6.
verify:
m = symbols('m')
r = (Rational('29.00') - Rational('13.40')) / 6
F = Rational('13.40') + r*(m - 4)
assert r == Rational(13, 5) and F.subs(m, 0) == 3
best = max(n for n in range(0, 50) if F.subs(m, n) <= 20)
assert best == 6
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [best]
